BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Festus tells Agrippa he has brought Paul before them, 'that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.' It is a judicial investigation — the formal hearing where the charges are sifted so the governor can write an honest report to Caesar.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for an examination carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the hearing — Festus needing something certain to write to his master about Paul.
